LESSON: READING 5.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading, part of Strand 5 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we read widely? 2. What materials do you enjoy reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. select appropriate reading materials for lifelong learning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. realise the importance of independent reading in lifelong learning.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. select appropriate reading materials for lifelong learning,

   Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency,

   Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment,

   Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. realise the importance of independent reading in lifelong learning.

   Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. select age-appropriate and high- interest reading materials such as narratives, poems, newspapers and magazines in print or electronic format,

2. set up an after-school club

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. select age-appropriate and high- interest reading materials such as narratives, poems, newspapers and magazines in print or electronic format,
2. set up an after-school club

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: This is developed as the learner uses selected reading materials from electronic sources.

• Learning to Learn: It is enhanced as the learner develops extensive reading strategies in their language clubs.

36

Values:
● Responsibility: This is cultivated as the learner engages diligently in assigned tasks on independent.

● Love: This is enhanced as the learner respects other learners' opinions when reading.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to link the concept of independent reading to Kiswahili.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. select appropriate reading materials for lifelong learning,
2. read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency,
3. apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment,
4. realise the importance of independent reading in lifelong learning.

Remember the key question: Why should we read widely? 2. What materials do you enjoy reading?
